title: Stable ordered fractions within 60-degree regions permit either sign of the ComCat shallow-share change in 2000-2025
abstract: We tested whether stable ordered depth-label fractions establish the sign of a shallow-share change when the fractions can differ by region. We used 12,848 global ComCat events with preferred M >= 5.5 and compared 2000-2012 with 2013-2025 at depth <= 15 km. We treated exact 10, 33, and 35 km records as uncertain and assumed that all other classifications were correct. One global set of time-stable ordered fractions permits a change of +1.43 to +12.68 percentage points. Separate stable ordered fractions in 18 fixed 60-degree regions permit -0.97 to +13.20 points. A shifted longitude grid also permits either sign. Thus the spatial scope of a calibration assumption changes the sign conclusion in this snapshot. These are sharp deterministic sensitivity bounds, not confidence limits or measured true depth changes. Untested order and time stability, other depth errors, mixed sources, and chosen periods limit inference. The package includes code, aggregate endpoint evidence, a separate exact-arithmetic audit, provenance, and a figure. External event records remain outside the signed package.

display.caption: Sharp shallow-share change bounds under global and regional stable ordered depth-label fractions. All bounds assume correct classifications outside exact 10, 33 and 35 km labels. These are permitted ranges, not confidence intervals.
